summary: Iteration 4 verifies the new EMAIL RECEIPT feature end-to-end. Completed a real Stripe TEST checkout in-browser for order o_6b5f3d609410 (product p-030 'Notion Workspace Template Pack (Pro)') as tbuyer1@example.com using card 4242 4242 4242 4242 12/34 CVC 123. Stripe redirected back to /payment/success and after auth-restored navigation the success panel rendered the receipt note (data-testid payment-receipt-note): 'A confirmation email with your secure download link has been sent.' GET /api/orders/{id}/receipt returns sent:false before payment and sent:true after with all required fields: to=tbuyer1@example.com, subject='Your ShahLance receipt — Notion Workspace Template Pack (Pro)', downloadUrl ends with /dashboard/buyer-orders, provider='placeholder', status='logged', sentAt ISO timestamp. Idempotency verified: 4 total status-polls produce only ONE email_receipts row (sentAt unchanged) and backend log shows exactly one '[EMAIL PLACEHOLDER] from=noreply@shahlance.com to=tbuyer1@example.com subject=...' line. Authorization: non-owner buyer -> 403, admin -> 200. Order flipped to paymentStatus=paid, status=processing, receiptSent=true. Download gating regression: GET /api/orders/{id}/download returns 404 'No deliverable file' for p-030 (no fileId — expected); existing test_download_after_paid still passes proving gating for products WITH files is intact. Full backend regression suite: 26/26 pytest tests PASS (added 2 receipt tests). No functional bugs.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to ~1027 lines and now also owns the receipt/email-send helper functions (_send_order_receipt, _mark_paid). Splitting payments + receipts into a dedicated router/service module is overdue.

email_receipts collection has no unique index on (orderId, session_id) — idempotency currently relies on the payment_transactions.emailSent flag; safe today, but a second checkout for the SAME order (retry after failed pay) would create a fresh transaction and thus a second receipt row. Consider indexing/upserting on order_id or on session_id.

_send_order_receipt uses the ORIGIN_URL stored on the payment_transaction (from body.origin_url passed by the frontend). A malicious/misconfigured client can therefore control the domain inside the emailed downloadUrl. Consider validating origin_url against an allowlist or using a server-side canonical FRONTEND_URL env.
Receipt HTML is stored fully in Mongo (html field of email_receipts) — fine for a placeholder but could bloat the collection; consider storing only a rendered summary + regenerating HTML on demand.

PaymentReturn shows 'View order' button but its href resolves to None in the DOM (likely client-side onClick navigation); consider using a real <Link> so it is right-clickable / middle-click openable — minor UX polish.
No brute-force / rate limit on /api/auth/login (pre-existing from iteration_2/3).
